1004689.etyen:
From tvang (“force, coercion”) + ekteskap (“marriage”), with linking -s- (“interfix”). The first element is derived from tvinge (“to force, compel”), and the second element is from Middle Low German echtschop (“marriage”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk tvangsekteskap, Swedish tvångsäktenskap and Danish tvangsægteskab (“forced marriage”).

1004945.etyen:
Borrowed from French espingole (“short, heavy firearm”), an alteration, probably influenced by Old Occitan espingola, of Old and Middle French Old French espringale (“dance; war engine”). The latter is generally derived from Old French espringaller (“to dance”), probably from a Germanic frequentative verb related to Middle Dutch springen (“to jump, spring”).
Ultimately from Frankish *springan (“to jump”), from Proto-West Germanic *springan (“to spring, jump”), from Proto-Germanic *springaną (“to jump; burst”), from Proto-Indo-European *sprenǵʰ- (“to move energetically, hurry, spring”).
